prompt: There is a view that the widespread use of computers and mobile phones has contributed to a decline in reading and writing abilities among young people. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often argued that the widespread use of computers and mobile phones has weakened young people's reading and writing skills. I completely disagree with this view because digital technology provides access to a wide range of reading materials and gives young people more opportunities to practise written communication.

On the one hand, computers and mobile phones have greatly expanded young people's access to reading materials. Instead of relying only on printed books and newspapers, students can now read e-books, online articles, academic journals and educational websites almost anywhere. For example, a university student can read an academic article on a mobile phone while travelling or waiting for a class. This makes reading more convenient and allows young people to encounter a wider range of vocabulary and ideas. As a result, digital technology can strengthen reading habits rather than necessarily weaken them.

Digital devices also give young people more opportunities to practise writing. Students regularly write emails, assignments and online discussions, while educational platforms can provide feedback from teachers. For instance, a student may submit an assignment online, receive comments about unclear sentences or grammatical errors, and then revise the work. This repeated process can gradually improve writing ability. Admittedly, excessive use of abbreviations in informal messages may have a negative effect on formal writing. However, when computers and phones are used for academic work and meaningful communication, they can actually support literacy skills.

In conclusion, I completely disagree that computers and mobile phones have generally caused a decline in young people's reading and writing abilities. When used appropriately, these devices provide greater access to reading materials and create valuable opportunities for written practice and feedback.
